scope: reconcile the known reliable-command format with the observed map-name offset

contradiction.if_body_starts_at_offset_0: opcode+seq occupy offsets 0..4, so a text command would begin at offset 5 and mp_cross_fire would appear at 5, not 15
contradiction.observed: mp_cross_fire sits at 15, i.e. ten bytes later than the simple opcode+seq layout predicts
what_the_ten_bytes_could_be: the command may carry a fixed 10-byte prefix before its text (for example a profile/delta header)
the packet may not be a plain text command at all but the binary service 2 form, where a u16 length and other fields precede the data
the first ten bytes may be genuinely key-shifted (contaminated), making the apparent 'opcode' at offset 10 meaningless

why_we_cannot_decide_yet: we do not have a byte-accurate frame from a CODOL-relevant source; the decrypted body is the only sample and its prefix is exactly the part the key shift obscures
next: capture a second gamestate from a fresh session and compare the contaminated prefix: fields that stay constant across sessions (like opcode) will be identifiable
capture the 206-byte client heartbeat body too and compare - if the server ever replies with a short text command, its clean prefix will reveal the layout

as an independent probe, emit opcode(1)+seq(1)+NUL text through our server and see whether the client at least acknowledges it - an ack would prove the text command path works even if the content is not a gamestate
